opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which Analyst does not. Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E016 (Ashley Roberts) as a contractor with basic security training, which contradicts the prior note listing full_time. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about E016's employment type: HR's note lists full_time, but the Security DB lists contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors with basic security training may have at most read access. Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, the maximum (read) is granted. I rely on the Security DB record for employment/security status, making read the appropriate level.
